newsitem.title: USA: Russian debt still down sharply after Lebed firing.
newsitem.headline: Russian debt still down sharply after Lebed firing.

text.p: Russian Vneshekonombank loans extended earlier losses after Russian President Boris Yelstin fired security chief Alexander Lebed, reflecting market nervousness, U.S. experts said.

"It's probably a little premature to give much insight, but the market right now seems to take it with a cautious tone," said Kurt Schmid, executive director at Swiss Bank Corp. "I would say the market has softened somewhat -- not dramatically since the news -- but it softened previously probably as a result of some power struggle."
Both S&P and Moody's said they had factored in the potential for political changes when they assigned Russia's credit ratings.
"I think the ratings were primarily based on a good credit story on improving fundamentals and a relatively successful macroeconomic stablization," added Schmid.

Meanwhile, Allen noted that the removal of Lebed should not have any impact on the closing of the Vnesh deal, which the market estimates at roughly $35 billion of loans. "I think people are expecting it around the end of the year but none of this should have any effect on the Vnesh closing," he said.
